simulation.organization_and_actors: Brazilian public or philanthropic hospital; bed-management coordinator, discharge nurse, pharmacist, attending physician, and internal-regulation team.
processes: coordinate discharge prerequisites across clinical review, medication reconciliation, transport, documents, follow-up, and bed release
recover blocked inpatient transfers and diagnostic or specialist handoffs
assemble and verify administrative prerequisites for regulated access without making clinical or eligibility decisions
simulation.baseline: Structured discharge and transfer checklists, protocol-based task queues, EHR workflow, deterministic prerequisites, role-based approvals, bed-management dashboards, alerts, escalation, and human clinical ownership.
simulation.remaining_gap: A bounded agent could gather status, call approved read tools, propose missing tasks, draft communications, and execute reversible administrative actions. However, the core pattern is mature workflow orchestration with tool calling; hospital-specific integrations, permissions, and safety gates are implementation adaptations rather than a differentiated opportunity.

portfolio_comparison.reason: The candidate repeats governed multi-step orchestration, retrieval, tool invocation, exception routing, checkpoints, and human approval already represented across the portfolio; changing the tools to EHR, bed, pharmacy, and transport systems does not create a new architectural spine.

existing_landscape.overlap: Current healthcare-agent platforms and enterprise agent builders already support healthcare-adapted orchestration, plugin selection, bounded workflow automation, and administrative discharge or bed-management assistance. Brazilian hospital regulation and patient-safety guidance require protocols, multiprofessional ownership, structured risk controls, and human clinical decisions.

where_ai_enters.primary_mechanism: A policy-governed agent retrieves current patient-flow context and invokes approved administrative tools to identify missing prerequisites, propose the next safe task, draft communication, and verify completion.
where_ai_enters.agent: Used only for bounded administrative coordination with allow-listed tools, explicit permissions, checkpoints, audit, and reversible actions.
where_ai_enters.llm: Interprets unstructured operational context and selects approved tools; it does not diagnose, prescribe, prioritize clinical urgency, authorize discharge, or allocate access autonomously.
where_ai_enters.human_control: Physicians, nurses, pharmacists, regulation teams, and bed managers retain clinical decisions, medication validation, discharge authorization, transfer acceptance, access prioritization, and exception resolution.
